thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PD-48721 fired for service=redis-prod-us-east-1 — symptom=MAXCLIENTS reached, threshold=95%, policy=auto-pager.

pagerduty-bot: Incident triggered, escalation policy: eng-oncall -> sre -> ops-lead. First pager sent to marina.

marina (oncall): acked. I'm on it — assigning to myself for triage.

marina (oncall): quick status: customer-facing errors spiking on /v1/generate (5xx ~12% over last 2m). Dashboards show Redis master connected_clients ~= maxclients and p99 op latency > 600ms.

kevin (sre): seeing the same. Remote regions (us-east) hit first. Looks like a connection storm rather than pure CPU/IO. Could be an app regression opening many persistent clients.

marina (oncall): running quick checks:
```
$ redis-cli -h redis-master-01 info clients | egrep "connected_clients|maxclients"
connected_clients:10002
maxclients:10002
```

marina (oncall): also checking pgbouncer pools for app-side DB impact (some services use Redis then Postgres):
```
$ kubectl exec -c pgbouncer pgbouncer-1 -- psql -c "SHOW POOLS;"
active_clients=180 idle_clients=5 max_client_conn=200
```

sam (backend): there was a new batch worker rollout ~5m ago that opens dedicated redis connections per shard. Rolling that back now but need a short mitigation for live traffic.

kevin (sre): mitigation plan: 1) apply short-term connection shedding on Redis by enabling client-side backoff (API gating) 2) switch read-heavy traffic to read-replicas where possible 3) temporarily reduce worker concurrency / rollback job (sam doing) 4) if needed, restart redis pod to clear clients (last resort).

sam (backend): rollback in progress — rolling job replicas to 0. Patch queued, will update in ~30s. Also adding per-worker connection cap in the rollback patch.

marina (oncall): applying API rate-limit for bulk endpoints:
```
# gateway rule
route /api/batch  -> rate_limit: 20r/s per token
```

kevin (sre): while rollback finishes, let's confirm eviction behavior and whether restarting will drop connections gracefully. If eviction doesn't free sockets, we may need to restart redis-master during low-traffic window.

marina (oncall): monitoring metrics: connected_clients trending down after rollback start (10002 -> 7420 -> 4120 over 2m). Error rate on /v1/generate also falling to ~2%. Good.

ops-lead: good call on rollback. Pager — do we have customer-facing impact? Need a short blurb for support.

marina (oncall): writing a quick customer note: "We experienced degraded API availability in us-east due to a client connection surge to Redis. Engineers rolled back a recent batch worker and applied rate limits; service is recovering and errors reduced. We will follow up with root cause and remediation." Will paste to support channel in 5m.

pagerduty-bot: marina acknowledged PD-48721. Escalation paused.

kevin (sre): post-rollback actions: add an alert for sustained connected_clients growth (rate of change) and per-deployment connection caps. Also add a graceful restart playbook that first rejects new connections via a firewall rule then restarts.

sam (backend): added PR to limit connections per worker and updated the job to use connection pooling (link: https://git.company/repo/pull/4521).

marina (oncall): performing a controlled redis slave promotion test to ensure failover path is healthy (no flapping). Results: promotion healthy, replicas caught up. No failover required.

kevin (sre): timeline note: root cause likely a bug in the new batch worker that created persistent client per shard and didn't close on errors — amplified during backlog processing. Fix is in PR and rollback blocked the surge fast enough to avoid restart.

ops-lead: escalate to postmortem. Assign to sam. Tentative mitigation items: connection caps, auto-scaling for workers with backpressure signals, alerting for client growth, circuit breaker on API for bulk ops.

marina (oncall): handing off monitoring and follow-up to kevin (sre) for the next hour — I'll remain on standby for any re-escalation. kevin: can you take PD follow-ups?

kevin (sre): taking handoff. I'll keep the PD incident open until metrics stable for 30m.

marina (oncall): support note posted to #customer-support: "Incident: Redis client surge in us-east briefly degraded API; rollback applied; errors reduced to baseline. No data loss. Follow-up postmortem and mitigation planned." :white_check_mark:

ops-lead: please prepare a short incident summary for execs once PD is closed. Include affected endpoints, % error, customers impacted (if any), and remediation timeline.

kevin (sre): metrics stable: connected_clients=1200 (baseline ~1000), 5xx <0.5%. I'll close PD in 40m if stable.

marina (oncall): closing notes: we've disabled the offending rollout, applied gateway rate limit, and validated replica health. PR to hard-limit worker connections merged.

kevin (sre): Incident resolved (PD-48721) — root cause: batch worker connection leak. Follow-ups: postmortem assigned, alerts and pooling changes merged, playbook update for redis client surges.

ops-lead: thanks team. Please add the postmortem ticket and any action items to the weekly SRE review.

marina (oncall): handing off fully; will check back in 30m. closing thread. :handshake:
